heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Bolivia
heroData.subtitle: Hire compliant talent in Bolivia without a local entity
heroData.description: Navigate Bolivian labor laws, severance mandates, and 13th-month bonuses with a compliant Employer of Record solution.
heroData.bestFor: Companies testing the Bolivian market or hiring remote support teams.

steps.title: Service Agreement
steps.description: Sign a Master Service Agreement (MSA) with the EOR provider. This defines the commercial terms, management fees (typically $200-$600/mo), and liability scope.

steps.title: Candidate Data Collection
steps.description: Gather employee details: CI (Identity Card), AFP registration (Pension Fund), and bank account information for salary deposits in BOB or USD.

steps.title: Employment Contract
steps.description: Draft a local compliant contract (Indefinite or Fixed-Term). Contracts must be registered with the Ministry of Labor (Ministerio de Trabajo) via the OVJS portal.

steps.title: Benefit Enrollment
steps.description: Enroll the employee in the Caja Nacional de Salud (CNS) for healthcare and the AFP (Pension Fund Administrators like Previsión or Futuro).

steps.title: First Payroll Run
steps.description: Process the first month's salary, ensuring deductions for RC-IVA (13%) and social security (12.71%) are accurately calculated.

items.title: Severance Mandates (Desahucio)
items.text: Termination without 'just cause' is expensive. You must pay 'Indemnización' (1 month/year of service) PLUS 'Desahucio' (3 months' salary lump sum penalty).

items.title: Infinite Contract Preference
items.text: Bolivian law heavily favors indefinite contracts. Fixed-term contracts are strictly regulated and cannot function as a probation period surrogate indefinitely.

items.title: 13th & 14th Month Pay
items.text: The 'Aguinaldo de Navidad' is mandatory. A second bonus ('Esfuerzo por Bolivia') triggers if annual GDP growth exceeds 4.5%, doubling the end-of-year burden.

faqs.question: Can I hire contractors instead of employees?
faqs.answer: It is risky. Misclassifying an employee as a civil contractor to avoid benefits can lead to retroactive claims for all unpaid social security, bonuses, and penalties.

faqs.question: Is a probation period allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes, a 3-month probation period is standard. During this time, termination can occur without payment of the 3-month Desahucio penalty, though proportional vacation/bonus may apply.

faqs.question: What documents are required for hiring?
faqs.answer: Locally, you need the Carnet de Identidad (CI), AFP registration number, and proof of address. Foreigners need a valid work visa or residency permit.

items.title: Cultural Norms
items.text: Relationships are crucial. Face-to-face meetings or personal video calls are preferred over impersonal emails.

items.title: Holidays
items.text: Bolivia has strict public holidays (Carnival, Census days, etc.) where work is legally prohibited or heavily surcharged.

items.title: Punctuality
items.text: While 'Hora Boliviana' (lateness) is a cultural stereotype, professional business meetings largely stick to schedule.

steps.title: Novelties Reporting
steps.description: Report changes by the 20th-25th: new hires, terminations, salary adjustments, overtime, and sick leave.

steps.title: Calculations & RC-IVA
steps.description: Calculate Gross-to-Net. Apply 12.71% employee SS deduction. Calculate RC-IVA (13%) tax base, deducting applicable VAT invoices presented by employees (Form 110).

steps.title: Payment & Pay Slips
steps.description: Disburse net salary to employees by the last day of the month or first days of the following month. Issue official pay slips (Boletad de Pago).

steps.title: Social Security Remittance
steps.description: Pay employer (16.71%) and employee (12.71%) contributions to the AFPs and Health Fund (CNS). Deadline is typically the next month.

steps.title: Tax Filing
steps.description: Submit RC-IVA (Form 608) to the Servicio de Impuestos Nacionales (SIN) if applicable.

items.title: RC-IVA Tax Shield
items.text: Employees can reduce their 13% RC-IVA tax liability by presenting VAT invoices (Form 110) for personal purchases. Payroll must process these deductions accurately.

items.title: Double Aguinaldo Risk
items.text: Always budget for the potential 'Segundo Aguinaldo'. If announced (usually in Oct/Nov based on GDP), it must be paid, non-prorated in some cases.

items.title: Minimum Wage 2025
items.text: The national minimum wage is set at BOB 2,750 (approx. $400 USD). This creates the floor for various benefit calculations and the RC-IVA non-taxable base.

faqs.question: What is the currency for payroll?
faqs.answer: Payroll MUST be calculated and reported in Bolivianos (BOB). Payments can be made in USD if agreed, but the pay slip must reflect the local currency equivalent.

faqs.question: Is sick leave paid?
faqs.answer: Yes. Short-term is paid by employer (first 3 days often). Long-term is covered by the Short-Term Social Security (Health Fund) subsidy, but the employer pays the contributions.

faqs.question: What is the seniority bonus?
faqs.answer: The 'Bono de Antigüedad' is a mandatory monthly bonus based on years of service and calculated on 3 minimum wages. It ranges from 5% (2-4 years) up to 50% (25+ years).

items.title: Banking Cutoffs
items.text: Bank transfers between different banks (ACH) are not instant and stop late afternoon. Same-bank transfers are recommended for urgency.

items.title: UFV Adjustments
items.text: Many tax values are adjusted daily by the UFV (Housing Promotion Unit), an inflation-indexed unit of account.

items.title: Printed Slips
items.text: Despite digital systems, many employees strongly prefer or legally require a physical, signed pay slip (Boleta de Pago) for their records.

items.title: Aguinaldo Load
items.text: Remember to add 8.33% to the Employer Total to account for the mandatory Christmas Bonus accrual.

items.title: Severance Load
items.text: Prudent employers accrue another 8.33% for Indemnización (Severance) as it is payable upon any termination after 90 days.

items.title: Solidarity 2
items.text: High earners (> BOB 13k, 25k, 35k) pay additional solidarity contributions ranging from 1% to 10%.

steps.title: Gross Salary
steps.description: Start with the monthly gross salary in BOB.

steps.title: Dduct Employee SS
steps.description: Subtract 12.71% from Gross.

steps.title: Calculate RC-IVA
steps.description: Apply RC-IVA logic (Gross - SS - 2xMinWage) * 13%. Deduct 13% of 2xMinWage and 13% of Form 110 invoices.

steps.title: Add Employer Costs
steps.description: Add 18.42% (SS) + 8.33% (Aguinaldo) + 8.33% (Indemnización) to the Gross to get Total Company Cost.

faqs.question: Does this include the Second Aguinaldo?
faqs.answer: No. The 'Esfuerzo por Bolivia' bonus is contingent on GDP growth and should be treated as a potential contingency, not a fixed cost.

faqs.question: Is the Seniority Bonus included?
faqs.answer: No, the 'Bono de Antigüedad' is separate and calculated on 3 National Minimum Wages percent depending on years served.

faqs.question: Are meal allowances taxed?
faqs.answer: Generally, yes, unless structured carefully. Most benefits in kind are considered part of the salary for social security.

items.title: Exchange Rate
items.text: The BOB is pegged to the USD (6.96), but 'street' rates or bank availability may vary. Calculations are always in Official BOB.

items.title: Retroactive Laws
items.text: Labor laws are protected by the constitution and principles of 'pro-worker', meaning interpretations often favor the employee retroactively.

items.title: Grossing Up
items.text: If negotiating 'Net Salary', be very careful with the gross-up calculation due to the complex RC-IVA deductions.

heroData.title: Company Incorporation in Bolivia
heroData.subtitle: Set up an SRL or SA
heroData.description: Establish a legal presence in Bolivia. Choose between limited liability (SRL) or corporation (SA) structures.
heroData.bestFor: Long-term market entry and large-scale hiring.

steps.title: Name Reservation
steps.description: Check availability and reserve the company name with the Commerce Registry (SEPREC - Servicio Plurinacional de Registro de Comercio).

steps.title: Draft Bylaws
steps.description: Draft the 'Acta de Constitución' (Articles of Incorporation) and have them notarized. This requires a Power of Attorney if shareholders are foreign.

steps.title: Register with SEPREC
steps.description: Submit notarized deeds to SEPREC to obtain the 'Matrícula de Comercio'. This grants the company legal personality.

steps.title: Tax Registration (SIN)
steps.description: Register with the National Tax Service (SIN) to obtain the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria).

steps.title: Municipal License
steps.description: Obtain the 'Licencia de Funcionamiento' from the local municipal government where the office is located.

items.title: SRL vs SA
items.text: SRL (LLC) is best for most subsidiaries. It requires 2-25 partners. SA (Corp) allows public share trading and requires a board of directors and a syndic.

items.title: Legal Rep Residency
items.text: The company MUST have a Legal Representative who is a Bolivian national or a foreigner with valid residency. They are personally liable for tax obligations.

items.title: Timeline Expectations
items.text: While paperwork can be done in 2-3 weeks, bank account opening is the bottleneck, often taking an additional 2-4 weeks due to strict compliance.

faqs.question: Can a foreign company own 100%?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you usually need at least 2 shareholders for an SRL. The second shareholder can hold a nominal 1% share.

faqs.question: Is a physical office required?
faqs.answer: Yes, you need a fiscal address for the NIT and Municipal License. A virtual office contract is often sufficient for service companies.

faqs.question: What is the minimum capital?
faqs.answer: No strict minimum for SRLs, but banks often prefer to see at least $500-$1,000 equivalent to justify the account.

items.title: Bureaucracy
items.text: Procedures (Trámites) often require patience. Systems may go offline, or officials may request physical photocopies ('fotocopias') of digital docs.

items.title: Notaries
items.text: Notaries in Bolivia are powerful. Their rubber stamp and signature are required for almost every corporate act.

items.title: Rubber Stamps
items.text: Get a company seal (sello) immediately. It is physically required to stamp invoices, letters, and contracts.

heroData.title: Staffing & Recruitment in Bolivia
heroData.subtitle: Find top talent in Cochabamba, La Paz, and Santa Cruz
heroData.description: Recruit software developers, bilingual support staff, and local professionals without agency fees for candidates.

steps.title: Job Requisition
steps.description: Define the role. For tech, English proficiency is a key differentiator. Verify salary benchmarks in BOB.

steps.title: Sourcing
steps.description: Use LinkedIn (popular for white-collar), Trabajos.bo, and local university job boards. Agencies leverage local networks in Santa Cruz and La Paz.

steps.title: Screening & Interview
steps.description: Conduct interviews. Technical assessments are common for dev roles. Verify cultural fit.

steps.title: Offer & Negotiation
steps.description: Present offer in Gross Monthly Salary (BOB). Clearly explain the 'Total Annual Cash' including the 13th month Aguinaldo to avoid confusion.

items.title: No Candidate Fees
items.text: It is strictly prohibited by Article 480 for agencies to charge fees to job seekers. All costs must be borne by the employer.

items.title: Tech Hub: Cochabamba
items.text: Cochabamba is known as the 'Silicon Valley of Bolivia'. It has a high density of software engineers and dev shops.

items.title: Offer Construction
items.text: Quote salaries in terms of 'Líquido Pagable' (Net Pay) estimates, as this is what employees care about, but contract in Gross.

faqs.question: Where should I post jobs?
faqs.answer: LinkedIn is best for professionals. Trabajos.bo and Facebook groups are very active for general roles.

faqs.question: Is English common?
faqs.answer: In the tech sector (Cochabamba/Santa Cruz), yes. In general administrative roles, bilingual talent commands a salary premium.

faqs.question: Can I background check?
faqs.answer: Yes, but data privacy laws apply. It is standard to ask for a 'Certificate of Good Conduct' (Antecedentes Policiales/Penales) which the candidate obtains.

items.title: Resume Format
items.text: Bolivian CVs often include personal details (photo, age, marital status) that are considered sensitive in the US/EU, but standard here.

items.title: References
items.text: Calling previous employers is a standard and expected part of the vetting process. Written references are less valued.

items.title: Family Ties
items.text: Nepotism can be common. Ensure strict conflict of interest policies if hiring multiple family members.

heroData.title: HRIS Solutions in Bolivia
heroData.subtitle: Manage Bolivian Workforces Digitally
heroData.description: Software platforms to handle attendance, payroll, and document management in compliance with Bolivian norms.

steps.title: Needs Assessment
steps.description: Determine if you need local payroll calculation (very specific to Bolivia) or just global HR record keeping.

steps.title: Vendor Selection
steps.description: Choose between local players (SALAR SOFTWARE) for tax compliance or global suites (Deel, ADP) for unified reporting.

steps.title: Data Migration
steps.description: Import employee data, specifically 'Fechas de Ingreso' (Start Dates) which are critical for the Seniority Bonus calculation.

steps.title: Training
steps.description: Train local HR staff. Ensure the system handles the 'Libro de Asistencia' (Attendance Book) requirements if digital.

items.title: Ministry Integration
items.text: A key feature for local HRIS is the ability to export reports compatible with the Ministry of Labor's 'OVJS' platform.

items.title: Attendance Tracking
items.text: Bolivia has strict overtime laws. Your HRIS must accurately log entry/exit times to calculate 'Horas Extras' and night surcharges.

items.title: Document Management
items.text: Store digital copies of signed contracts, pay slips, and the Finiquito forms. Electronic signatures are legally valid if certified (ADSIB).

faqs.question: Is digital signature accepted?
faqs.answer: Yes, under Law 164. However, it requires a recognized digital certificate issued by an authorized entity (e.g., ADSIB).

faqs.question: Can I use Excel?
faqs.answer: For very small teams, yes. But manual calculation of the seniority bonus and tax shield (Form 110) limits is prone to errors.

faqs.question: Does it connect to banks?
faqs.answer: Advanced local systems generate the .txt files required for bulk salary uploads to major banks like BNB, Mercantil, or BISA.

items.title: Internet Stability
items.text: While cities have fiber, remote areas rely on mobile data. Ensure your self-service portal is mobile-friendly and lightweight.

items.title: Biometrics
items.text: Biometric attendance (fingerprint) is the gold standard for proving labor hours in court cases.

items.title: Backup Data
items.text: Keep local backups. Cloud-only solutions can be risky if internet outages occur on payroll cutoff days.

heroData.title: Accounting in Bolivia
heroData.subtitle: Bookkeeping, Tax Filing, and Audit
heroData.description: Ensure compliance with Bolivian GAAP, monthly VAT/IT filings, and annual financial statement submission.

steps.title: Document Collection
steps.description: Gather all physical and digital invoices (Facturas). Bolivia has a mix of electronic and manual billing.

steps.title: VAT & IT Calculation
steps.description: Calculate VAT (13% Debit vs Credit) and Transaction Tax (3% on Gross Income). Prepare Form 200 and 400.

steps.title: Filing & Payment
steps.description: File declarations via the SIAT system. Payment is due based on the last digit of the NIT (Tax ID).

steps.title: Bookkeeping Entry
steps.description: Record transactions in the Daily Book and Ledger, maintained in Spanish and Bolivianos as per Commercial Code.

items.title: Transaction Tax (IT)
items.text: The 3% IT is a tax on GROSS revenue, not profit. It applies to almost every transaction. CIT payments can serve as an offset (pago a cuenta) for IT in future periods.

items.title: Bancarization
items.text: Transactions over BOB 50,000 must be backed by banking documents to be deductible. These must be reported in the 'Bancarización' module.

items.title: Fiscal Year Ends
items.text: Not all companies use Dec 31. Industrial: Mar 31. Ag/Cattle: Jun 30. Mining: Sep 30. Banking/Comm/Services: Dec 31.

faqs.question: Can I keep books in USD?
faqs.answer: For internal reporting, yes. But legal books MUST be legally kept in Bolivianos (BOB) and Spanish.

faqs.question: Do I need an audit?
faqs.answer: Yes, if annual revenue exceeds approx. $170,000 USD (limit set by Registry), you must submit audited financial statements.

faqs.question: What is the LC-IVA?
faqs.answer: Libro de Compras y Ventas. It's the detailed registry of all invoices that supports the VAT declaration. It must be sent digitally.

items.title: Bill Everything
items.text: Every expense needs a 'Factura' with your NIT and Name. Generic receipts are non-deductible.

items.title: QR Payments
items.text: QR payments (Simple) are ubiquitous and valid for business, provided they are backed by an invoice.

items.title: Physical Archive
items.text: Keep physical copies of major contracts and invoices for 8 years. Tax audits often demand the original paper.

steps.title: Update Matrícula
steps.description: Renew the Commercial Registry (Matrícula de Comercio) annually at SEPREC. Requires filing the previous year's financials.

steps.title: Holding AGM
steps.description: Hold the Annual General Meeting (Junta Ordinaria) to approve financials and board actions within 3 months of year-end.

steps.title: Municipal License Payment
steps.description: Pay the annual municipal business license fee (Patente Municipal) to the local alcaldía.

steps.title: Update ROE
steps.description: Update the 'Registro Obligatorio de Empleadores' (ROE) with the Ministry of Labor quarterly and submit the 'Planillas'.

items.title: Labor Book stamping
items.text: The 'Libro de Asistencia' and other labor books must be physically or digitally stamped/approved by the Ministry. Neglect leads to fines.

items.title: UBO Reporting
items.text: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) disclosure is increasingly required by banks and potentially tax authorities to combat money laundering.

items.title: Virtual Office
items.text: Ensure your providers for virtual offices maintain the Municipal License active. If they fail, your NIT (Tax ID) might be blocked.

faqs.question: What if I miss the Registry renewal?
faqs.answer: You face fines and your company is marked as 'inactive' or 'depurada', preventing you from bidding on contracts or changing bylaws.

faqs.question: Can the Legal Rep be foreign?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they MUST hold valid residency (Carnet de Extranjería) to represent the company before the Tax Authority (SIN).

faqs.question: How long to close a company?
faqs.answer: Liquidation is complex and can take 12-24 months due to the need for tax clearance (Fiscalización) from the SIN.

items.title: Signage
items.text: You must display your 'NIT' certificate and any licenses visibly in your office premises to avoid municipal fines.

items.title: Whistleblowing
items.text: Employees can report non-compliance anonymously to the Ministry of Labor, triggering surprise inspections.

items.title: Digital Folder
items.text: Maintain a 'Carpeta Digital' with scanned PDFs of all compliance docs (Roe, Fundempresa/Seprec, Nit, License) for quick access.

items.title: IT and IUE Offset
items.text: IUE paid can be used as a credit against future IT payments. This effectively means you don't pay IT *if* your IUE payment covers it, until the credit runs out.

items.title: Transfer Pricing
items.text: Transactions with related parties abroad must follow arm's length principles. Transfer pricing studies are required for significant volumes.

items.title: Zero-Rate VAT 2025
items.text: Specific incentives for capital goods imports may apply zero-rate VAT. Check Supreme Decrees for updated lists of machinery.

steps.title: Monthly (VAT & IT)
steps.description: File Form 200 (VAT) and Form 400 (IT) monthly. Due date depends on last digit of NIT (e.g., ends in 0 = 13th of month).

steps.title: Quarterly (RC-IVA)
steps.description: Form 608 for employee withholding is typically processed monthly, but consultants file quarterly.

steps.title: Annual (IUE)
steps.description: File Form 500 and pay annual Corporate Income Tax within 120 days of fiscal year end.

steps.title: Annual (Financials)
steps.description: Submit digital financial statements (Form 605) via SIAT.

faqs.question: Is VAT refundable?
faqs.answer: Exporters can claim CEDEIMs (Tax Return Certificates) to get VAT refunds, but the process is bureaucratic and lengthy.

faqs.question: What is the ITF?
faqs.answer: Impuesto a las Transacciones Financieras. It charges 0.30% on debits/credits in foreign currency (USD) to encourage usage of BOB.

faqs.question: Are digital services taxed?
faqs.answer: Yes, VAT generally applies to services consumed in Bolivia, even if provided from abroad, though enforcement varies.

items.title: UFV Indexing
items.text: Tax debts are indexed to the UFV (Unidad de Fomento de Vivienda). Delaying payment even by a day increases the debt due to inflation.

items.title: Frozen Accounts
items.text: The SIN (Tax Authority) has the power to freeze business bank accounts (retención de fondos) rapidly for unpaid debts.

items.title: Perdonazos
items.text: Occasionally, the government issues tax amnesties ('Perdonazos') waiving interest and penalties. Watch for these if you have old liabilities.

heroData.title: M&A Services in Bolivia
heroData.subtitle: Advisory and Due Diligence
heroData.description: Navigate mergers, acquisitions, and joint ventures in Bolivia. Protect against hidden labor and tax liabilities.

steps.title: Preliminary Deal
steps.description: Letter of Intent (LOI) and NDA. Defines the scope and exclusivity.

steps.title: Due Diligence (Key)
steps.description: Deep dive into Tax (open years), Labor (unpaid benefits/severance risk), and Corporate (validity of shares) status.

steps.title: SPA Drafting
steps.description: Share Purchase Agreement. Must be notarized. Share transfers in SRLs require public deed and registry modification.

steps.title: Closing & Registry
steps.description: Payment and registration of the new owners in the Commercial Registry (SEPREC). 3% Transaction Tax is exempt for share sales.

items.title: Labor Successor Liability
items.text: Acquirers often inherit all labor liabilities. Given the cost of 'Desahucio', checking for hidden dismissals or misclassified contractors is vital.

items.title: Tax Statute of Limitations
items.text: The statute of limitations is 8 years. Due diligence should cover this entire period for tax contingencies.

items.title: Escrow Usage
items.text: It is common to hold back 10-20% of the price in Escrow for 12-24 months to cover post-closing indemnity claims.

faqs.question: Is share sale taxed?
faqs.answer: The PROFIT on the sale is subject to taxes (Capital Gains, often treated as income 25% for companies). The transaction itself is exempt from the 3% IT.

faqs.question: Can I merge an SRL and SA?
faqs.answer: Yes, Bolivian Commercial Code allows transformation and merger of different entity types.

faqs.question: Is antitrust approval required?
faqs.answer: Yes, for transactions that lead to market dominance or concentration, filing with the AEMP (Empresas Authority) may be required.

items.title: Family Businesses
items.text: Most Bolivian companies are family-owned. Deal-making often involves navigating family dynamics and informal decision structures.

items.title: Informality
items.text: Target companies may have 'informal' practices (unregistered sales). Valuations must discount these as they cannot be legally recognized.

items.title: Currency Controls
items.text: Large USD transfers may face scrutiny or delays. Ensure all capital flows are properly registered with the Central Bank if applicable.

heroData.title: Software Development in Bolivia
heroData.subtitle: The Silicon Valley of the Andes
heroData.description: Leverage high-quality, English-speaking tech talent from Cochabamba and Santa Cruz at competitive rates.

items.title: Cochabamba Hub
items.text: Cochabamba hosts the largest concentration of software houses (Jala, Jalasoft, TruExtend), fostering a strong ecosystem of Java and .NET talent.

items.title: Time Zone
items.text: Bolivia (GMT-4) aligns perfectly with US Eastern Time (ET), allowing for real-time collaboration without jet lag.

items.title: English Proficiency
items.text: Tech professionals in export-oriented firms generally have high English proficiency due to the industry's focus on US clients.

steps.title: Staff Augmentation
steps.description: Hire dedicated devs who work as part of your team. Billed monthly/hourly.

steps.title: Project Outsourcing
steps.description: Fixed-price or T&M contracts for specific deliverables (MVP, App, Module).

steps.title: Build-Operate-Transfer
steps.description: Vendor builds the team, operates it, and transfers legal ownership to you after 18-24 months.

faqs.question: What is the turnover rate?
faqs.answer: Turnover is moderate. Competitive salaries from US startups are increasing competition, but loyalty in established local firms remains good.

faqs.question: Are there tax incentives?
faqs.answer: Yes, Law 164 and recent decrees offer some incentives for software export, often zero-rating VAT for service exports.

faqs.question: Top skills available?
faqs.answer: Strong availability of Java, .NET, JavaScript (React/Node), and mobile (Android/iOS) developers.

items.title: Loyalty
items.text: Bolivian developers are known for high retention rates compared to neighboring markets, provided the culture is good.

items.title: Nearshore
items.text: The cultural alignment with the US is strong in the tech sector. Many devs have worked with US clients for years.

items.title: Equipment
items.text: Importing laptops can be expensive due to customs. It's often better to buy locally or provide a stipend.

heroData.title: Marketing Agencies in Bolivia
heroData.subtitle: Digital, Social, and Brand
heroData.description: Connect with local consumers through Bolivian agencies specializing in social media and digital campaigns.

items.title: Facebook Dominance
items.text: Facebook is the absolute dominant platform in Bolivia, used for everything from commerce (Marketplace) to news.

items.title: Advertising Law 453
items.text: Misleading advertising is strictly penalized. Promotions involving prizes ('Sorteos') require tedious pre-authorization from the AJ (Gaming Authority).

items.title: WhatsApp Marketing
items.text: WhatsApp is key for B2C conversion. Local consumers expect to be able to close sales or ask questions via WhatsApp.

steps.title: Localization
steps.description: Adapt content. Bolivian Spanish is standard, but colloquialisms vary between 'Camba' (East) and 'Colla' (West) regions.

steps.title: Channel Selection
steps.description: Prioritize Facebook and TikTok for B2C. LinkedIn is growing for B2B but still niche.

steps.title: AJ Authorization
steps.description: If running a contest/giveaway, submit rules to the Autoridad de Fiscalización del Juego (AJ) weeks in advance.

steps.title: Launch & Moderate
steps.description: Launch ads. Active community management is crucial as Bolivians comment frequently on ads.

faqs.question: Can I pay ads in BOB?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the ad account is set up locally. However, international card payments may incur the 0.3% ITF or currency exchange fees.

faqs.question: Is influencer marketing big?
faqs.answer: Yes, micro-influencers on TikTok and Instagram are very cost-effective for reaching younger demographics.

faqs.question: What is the ad tax?
faqs.answer: Foreign digital services (like Meta/Google ads) often technically attract VAT, but collection mechanisms vary.

items.title: WhatsApp First
items.text: For many consumers, WhatsApp IS the internet. Ensure your marketing funnel leads to a WhatsApp conversation.

items.title: Gaming Authority
items.text: Never run a 'Like and Share to Win' contest without AJ authorization. Fines are steep and competitors will report you.

items.title: Video Content
items.text: Short-form video (TikTok/Reels) sees the highest engagement. Static images are less effective in the current market.
